u18.title: If the person is under 18
u18.lead: This needs special care. Please use only the official child-safety routes below.
u18.dont.title: Do not save, forward or screenshot the content
u18.dont.body: Even to show the police, keep only the links, usernames and dates. Saving or sharing sexual images of a child is a crime, even when you are trying to help.
u18.ncrp: Report on cybercrime.gov.in. It has a section for crimes against children, and you can report without giving your name for this kind of content.
u18.tid: If the photo or video is of someone under 18, NCMEC's Take It Down can stop it spreading on partner platforms without the image leaving the device.
u18.adult: If you are a parent or teacher: stay calm, listen, and tell the child it is not their fault.

tracker.title: Platform Accountability Tracker
tracker.label: Prototype methodology, author-assessed
tracker.sub: 8 platforms scored out of 100 on public, checkable criteria. Every point links to its evidence. Where we could not check something, it says Not assessed.
tracker.sort.name: Name
tracker.evidenceEnglish: Evidence is shown in English, as in the sources.
tracker.noIncidents: No incidents logged for this platform.
tracker.corrections: Spotted an error? Send a correction with a source.
tracker.pickMore: Pick at least 2 platforms to compare.
tracker.method.gradesBody: A 85 to 100, B 70 to 84, C 55 to 69, D 40 to 54, F below 40. The grade uses the share of assessed points, and is shown only when at least 5 of 8 criteria are assessed.
tracker.method.evidenceBody: Each fact comes from a public source: the platform's own policy pages, the StopNCII partner list, the government's list of Grievance Officers, regulator announcements and major investigations. Every criterion shows its source and the date it was checked. Totals and grades are computed in code, never typed by hand.
tracker.method.limitsBody: This is a prototype scored by one author from public information, not an audit. Some criteria need hands-on testing and are marked Not assessed. A lower-bound rule applies: where we could not confirm a detail (for example, whether a form works without an account), we give the lower score and say so. Scores will be re-checked before any public launch.
tracker.inc.window: C8 counts NCII-related failures in the 12 months before the review date.

support.sub: You do not have to do this alone. These are official services. Numbers were checked on government sites.
support.emotionalBody: Shock, shame, anger and fear are normal reactions. Talk to someone you trust, take breaks, and remember that this was done to you, not by you.
support.legalBody: One Stop Centres can connect you with legal aid. Your District Legal Services Authority also offers free legal help to women.
support.notCrisis: Reclaim is not a crisis counselling service.
insights.title: Insights
insights.sub: How a public dashboard could measure platform response. These charts use 200 synthetic reports.
insights.missed: Share of reports that missed the 2-hour deadline
insights.whyBody: No one publishes how fast platforms remove NCII in India. If victims could share response times anonymously and by choice, a dashboard like this could hold platforms to the 2-hour rule. The future research paper will propose these metrics.
about.title: About Reclaim
about.lead: Reclaim is a free, privacy-first web app for people in India whose intimate, morphed or AI-generated images are shared without consent.
about.whyBody: Every platform has a different report form, most people do not know about the 2-hour rule or the Grievance Officer, and shame stops people from asking for help. Reclaim puts all of it in one calm place, and publicly scores how well platforms protect victims.
about.privacyBody: Reclaim has no accounts, no database, no analytics, no cookies and no third-party scripts or fonts. It never asks for, uploads or stores any image. What you type is saved only in this browser's local storage, under one key, and 'Delete everything' removes it.
about.limitsBody: Reclaim explains the law in plain words and links to official sources, each with a 'last verified' date. It is not legal advice, it does not file anything for you, and it is not a crisis service. There is no lawyer on the team yet; review by a cyber-law expert and a survivor-support NGO is the first step on the roadmap.
about.demoBody: The demo case, 'Ananya S.', is fictional. Every handle, link and ID in it is obviously fake (demo_ prefixes, example.com, DEMO- IDs). The Insights charts use synthetic data.
about.builtBody: A static Next.js site on Vercel. Content lives in versioned JSON and Markdown files validated at build time. User data lives only in the browser.
about.contactBody: If a platform, lawyer or reader spots an error, please open an issue with a source on the project's GitHub page.
tour.label: Guided tour
tour.1: Reclaim starts here. A scared person taps 'Get help now'. Let's see what happens next.
tour.2: The help flow asks one question per screen. For the demo, Ananya's answers are filled in: an AI-morphed image on Telegram, reposted on X and Instagram.
tour.3: Her answers become an ordered action plan: save evidence, report on each platform, file on the cybercrime portal, escalate if the 2-hour deadline passes.
tour.4: Each platform has exact steps, the official form and the India Grievance Officer route. Telegram has no web form and no dedicated NCII policy.
tour.5: The drafter writes a ready-to-paste NCRP complaint from her case, with the legal sections that may apply. Nothing is sent anywhere.
tour.6: The case tracker shows the 2-hour countdown. Telegram has missed the deadline, so Reclaim offers an escalation. X removed the post, but 28 hours late.
tour.7: The public scorecard rates 8 platforms on checkable criteria. Every point links to its evidence.
tour.8: The Learn hub explains NCII, deepfakes and rights in plain English and Hindi. That's the tour. Exit the demo to start a real plan.
